added_lines: diocesan appointments - this weekend is fr lagan’s last weekend in our parish as our priest, i take the opportunity to thank him sincerely for his work both in the parish and the hospitals over the past four years. his endearing personality enabled him to get to know many people in a short period of time. his good humour and generosity of time have brought many blessings to many people and our parish community. as he begins a new phase of his life as parish priest in the sperrin parishes of gortin and greencastle, i on behalf of the parish, wish him every blessing. it will be a very big change for him so let’s keep him and all the priests involved in the latest diocesan appointments in our prayers. words of thanks from fr lagan on 18th august 2022, bishop donal mckeown appointed me to the parishes of glendermott and strathfoyle. on that occasion, even though it was a change, i very much knew that i was coming home. i was sent to a parish that i had previously served and for a short while after my ordination in 2012 began ministering as a priest. it is a place that i love very much and this last four years have been both a time of immense blessing. on 9th october, bishop router appointed me to the parishes of greencastle and gortin in co tyrone. whilst i am deeply honoured for his trust in me, i leave here with the best preparation i could ask for in taking up this new challenge. i want to thank all the staff of our parish, those who work to support the running of glendermott and strathfoyle, but especially to fr joshi for his kindness, guidance, support and friendship and to fr michael canny for his ever willing example, paternal guidance and endless patience not only during my time here but throughout my priestly ministry and also to each of you, for your prayers, your faith filled example and for the love and kindness that you have shown me, i will forever treasure. please keep me in your prayers and be assured of my prayers for you, your loved ones and families in the months and years ahead. thank you. baptisms – we welcome into god’s family: noah doherty birch hill, cailean john christopher tracey deramore drive. anniversaries – for those whose anniversaries occur around this time molly hegarty, nora brown, margaret flynn, jim mellon, fonsy doherty, bob kelly, joseph devine, william barr, willie guthrie, paul mcfadden, john monaghan, charlie mullan, william mcconomy, bill and kathleen monk, mary storey, brian simpson, lawerence boyle. offertory collections: glendermott: £3,800.00 strathfoyle: parishes of glendermott & strathfoyle sunday 25th october 2026 thirtieth sunday in ordinary time the commandment of love is the greatest of the commandments, the mother of all the virtues, and the pulsating heart of the christian message. we are created in the image of a god who is love; so, we cannot live without love in today’s gospel reading from matthew, one of the pharisees, a lawyer, asks jesus to identify ‘the greatest commandment of the law’(mt 22:36). in response, jesus quotes the great ‘shema’ prayer recited daily by all devout jews (cf. deut 6:4-5). this prayer exhorts us to love god with our whole heart, mind and soul. jesus immediately adds a second commandment, familiar to his audience namely, ‘love your neighbour as yourself’ (mt 22:39). sadly, the word ‘love’ is so overused in our world today that it has lost much of its meaning. we speak of love of country, love of sport, love of food, love between friends, love of parents, romantic love, etc as pope leo teaches, ‘true love is not merely a fleeting, briefly inflamed emotion. it is more. it is a deep commitment to the other, a decision, a journey and a covenant for life all genuine love is manifested in action; it is practical and outgoing. in the words of st augustine: ‘it has the hands to help others. it has the feet to hasten to the poor and needy. it has the eyes to see misery and want. it has the ears to hear the sighs and sorrows of people.’ such love is demanding. it summons us to leave our comfort zones, to give our time, our energy, our talents, and, indeed, our very selves to others feast of all saints mass arrangements for the feast of all saints- saturday 31st october 6:00pm church of immaculate conception 6:00pm st. oliver plunkett 6:30pm st. columb’s church (note change of time) waterside strathfoyle amalgamated)

the church of our lady of lourdes serving the parishes of steelstown & culmore sunday 1st november 2026 all saints plenary indulgence from 12 noon on 1 november until midnight on 2 november all who have confessed, received holy communion and prayed for the pope’s intentions (one our father and hail mary, or any other prayer of one’s choice) can gain one plenary indulgence by visiting a church or oratory and there reciting one our father and the apostle’s creed. this indulgence is applicable only to the souls of the departed. confession may be made at any time within the week preceding or the week following 1 november. holy communion may be received on any day from 1 november to 8 november. the faithful who vis it a cemetery and pray for the dead may gain a plenary indulgence applicable only to the holy souls on the usual conditions once per day from 1 to 8 november. the conditions mentioned above apply also for this. a prayer for the dead lord, be with us in these november days of darkness. in our anxiety and fear he lp us to remember that death is the dawning of eternal life. give to those who have died freedom from pain and bring them to the peace of heav en. in moments of sadness may we experience the closeness of your friendship and may we always know the strength of your presence. we ask this through christ our lord. amen confessions weekend saturday: after 10am mass; 5.45pm – 6.25pm sunday: 10.30am – 10.50am weekdays monday : 6.30pm – 6.55pm tuesday : 8.10am – 8.30am thursday : 9.30am – 09.50am mass times sundays vigil: 6.30pm sunday: 09.00am; 11.00am; 12.15pm weekdays monday – friday: 7.45am monday: 7.00pm tuesday – saturday: 10.00am devotions eucharistic adoration thursday: 08.00 – 09.55am 10.30am – 12 noon rosary before 10am mass divine mercy chaplet after 10am mass steelstown

. craft fair - carnhill community centre, (thewee grey hut), are holding a christmas craft fair on saturday the 7 november 2026. 11am.-3pm. £1 admission, children under 11 are free. please su pport your local craftworkers. pope’s intention for november - for the proper use of wealth. let us pray for the proper use of wealth, that not succumbing to the temptation of selfishness, it may always be at the service of the common good and solidarity of those who have less. remembering our faithful departed 1 november the feast of all saints sunday 1 nov is the feast of all saints. mass times are 9am, 11am and 12.15pm. monday 2 november all souls day monday 2 nov is all souls day. mass times are 7.45am, 10am and 7pm. parishioners and friends who have died since november last year will have a s pecial place in our prayer on monday 16th november. their names will be read out at the 7pm mass on monday 16th. during this mass, the names of those who died in the past year will be called out, and a member of each fa mily will be invited to bring forward a candle for their loved one.

or by calling (028) 79386259. lectio divina – join us on thursday evenings at 8:00pm in st columb’s church for our weekly praying of the sacred scriptures. centring prayer group – join us on wednesday at 8:00pm in the st columb’s church (parish hall) unlocking the mystery of the bible many of us want to read the bible but can find it difficult to understand. the parish will be running ‘unlocking the mystery of the bible’, an eight-part course that will help us to understand the main story of the bible and how all the different parts fit together. it gives the ‘big picture’ and helps us see what the bible is really about. we will meet on monday evenings starting on 2nd november at 8pm (after 7.30pm mass) in the parish hall, st columb’s church. sessions will begin with prayer, followed by a video presentation and small group discussion. by the end, you’ll feel more confident reading the bible and have a better understanding of how you fit into god’s plan. to register for the course, please leave your name and contact details at the parish office (028 71 342303 or email
